# Layout revision report — Sample Hall A (40m x 30m)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

## Before / after

Identical conditions for every iteration: scenario `entry`, 200 agents, 300 s, seed 42, density grid 2 m (fingerprint `2d16dacf`). Target: max density ≤ 2 p/m² with no validation errors.

| Metric | Baseline (iteration 0) | Final (iteration 2) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max density | 3.21 p/m² | 1.83 p/m² | −1.38 p/m² (−42.9%) |
| p90 travel time | 133.8 s | 101.9 s | −31.9 s (−23.8%) |
| Mean travel time | 88.3 s | 75.5 s | −12.8 s (−14.5%) |
| Completed fraction | 99.6% | 100% | +0.4 pt |
| Hotspots | 1 | 0 | −1 |
| Validation errors | 0 | 0 | ±0 |

Stop reason: **target met** — max density 1.831 ≤ target 2 p/m² with no validation errors.

## Design brief (initial constraints)

Indoor hall with moderate attendance for its floor area: the standard aisle width and door clearance apply and booths are not yet pushed away from the entrance. The first simulation will show whether the entrance area needs more room.

- Default constraints kept.

Booth coordinates were then computed by the layout solver under these constraints.

## What changed and why

**Revision after iteration 0 → 1.** High-attraction booth B03 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds.

- popular_door_distance 0 → 12 m

**Revision after iteration 1 → 2.** Hotspot #0 persists next to B03, which shares the zone with other high-attraction booths; moving it north separates their visitor crowds.

- B03 target (25, 13) → (25, 19)

## Iteration history

| Iteration | Max density (p/m²) | p90 travel (s) | Completed | Errors | Comparable |

| 0 | 3.21 | 133.8 | 99.6% | 0 | yes |
| 1 | 2.38 | 112.2 | 100% | 0 | yes |
| 2 | 1.83 | 101.9 | 100% | 0 | yes |

## Assumptions

- Pedestrian metrics come from the **mock engine** (synthetic density field for demo purposes, not a pedestrian simulation); one scenario and seed per run, so results are a single sample, not a distribution.
- Booth popularity values are planning estimates of relative attraction, taken as given.
- Densities are peak values per grid cell over the run; hotspot thresholds are the engine's. Travel times count finished agents only.
- Geometric checks cover booth/obstacle/door-clearance/aisle rules only; egress capacity, fire code and accessibility were not assessed.
- Analysis and revision proposals by `stub`; all metrics and coordinates in this report are computed by tools.

## Unconfirmed items

- Emergency door D-emg swing direction unconfirmed (from floor plan)

# Layout revision report — Sample Hall A (40m x 30m)

> This is a planning draft produced by an AI agent from simulation output. It is not a permit, fire-code or crowd-safety certification; a qualified reviewer must confirm it against the venue's actual conditions and applicable regulations.

## Summary

Design brief: Indoor hall with moderate attendance for its floor area: the standard aisle width and door clearance apply and booths are not yet pushed away from the entrance. The first simulation will show whether the entrance area needs more room. The solver placed the booths of Sample Hall A (40m x 30m) under those constraints and the layout was simulated under one fixed scenario. The worst congestion is hotspot #0, close to the main entrance. High-attraction booth B03 draws visitors into this zone right where the entrance inflow arrives, so arriving and browsing crowds overlap.

Across 2 revisions it kept the layout as stable as possible and changed only what the simulation pointed at: High-attraction booth B03 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds; then Hotspot #0 persists next to B03, which shares the zone with other high-attraction booths; moving it north separates their visitor crowds. Each revised layout was re-validated and re-simulated with the identical scenario, so the before/after comparison below reflects layout changes only.

The run stopped because: max density 1.831 ≤ target 2 p/m² with no validation errors. Treat the result as a planning draft for human review; the items under Unconfirmed must be checked on site before the plan is relied on.
